title: Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan Missed-Recovery Review and Its Recording
content:
**Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan — the review of a payday whose recovery fell short.**

## Scope

The missed-recovery review governs the tier review of the plan's latest closed payday, the pay date of its latest period close line, when a shortfall carries a pay date on or after the plan's level effective date, a payday no review has yet covered; the latest such pay date is the shortfall payday, and a plan without such a shortfall is reviewed under the tier review instead.

## When the review is owed

Each payday is reviewed once and only after it has closed: the review of the latest closed payday is recorded no earlier than the day after that payday, once that payday's payroll settlement and any write-off booked on it are on the plan, and it is owed only while the plan's level effective date is on or before that payday. A recorded review leaves the level effective date the day after the payday it covers, so a review recorded late, even on or after the next payday, never makes the next payday's review fall due or lapse. When a later payday's period close is booked before an earlier payday's review is recorded, the one review of the latest closed payday covers every payday since the level effective date. This replaces, for every review under the missed-recovery review, the former rule that the plan tier is reviewed each payday after that payday's recoveries and any shortfall are booked.

## Effect of a recorded review

The tier a missed-recovery review sets applies to transfers booked from the day after the payday reviewed, and that day is recorded as the plan's level effective date, whatever day the review is recorded, a transfer or fee already booked when the review is recorded keeping the terms in force when it was booked.

*Hypothetical:* the review of a payday of 13 June recorded on 17 June records 14 June as the level effective date.

## Recording the review: `record_missed_recovery_review_3a64d9dd`

**Capability.** Records the review of a worker's Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan for a payday whose recovery fell short. One call sets the plan's tier to the tier that review lands on and records the date from which that tier applies to new transfers. The worker sees the tier and its effective date on the plan at once; transfers already booked are not changed.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `record_missed_recovery_review_3a64d9dd` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `access_plan_id` | the reference number of the worker's Earned Wage Access Plan, read from the plan record looked up for this worker | identifier text |
| `new_variant_name` | the tier the review lands on | exactly one of `Paystride Access Starter` (entry tier), `Paystride Access Standard` (second tier), `Paystride Access Plus` (third tier), `Paystride Access Preferred` (fourth tier), `Paystride Access Premier` (fifth tier); `Paystride Access Premier Plus` in no situation, since this review never lands above the tier one below the tier held (a plan already on Paystride Access Starter stays on it), and that value is refused with an error |
| `level_effective_date` | the calendar date from which the tier applies to transfers booked on or after it; transfers already booked keep their terms | a real calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD, Eastern Time |

**Return.** A confirmation sentence carrying the plan reference, the tier now held (its full tier name), the previously held tier (its full tier name) and the date it applies from (YYYY-MM-DD); the sentence's presence means the review is recorded. Explicit errors: an unknown tier name; `Paystride Access Premier Plus`; a `level_effective_date` that is not a real calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD; no plan with the given `access_plan_id`. On an error nothing is recorded.
